comment: URGENT Homeless Problem in Fairmont Park Attachment #4 & #5 Council Comments Email Hello. My name is Katia Graftieaux and I recently purchased a home in Sugar House, near Fairmont Park, in October 2021. I moved here from San Francisco, where the homelessness was unbelievable. I literally had hundreds people sleeping, defecating and doing drugs on my doorstep. Over the last eight months living in Salt Lake City, homelessness has increased rapidly in my neighborhood, specifically in Fairmont Park, go from bad to worse. I was aware of the homeless problem on the east side of the park before the liquor stores when I moved here. What I can't understand is why the City is allowing all the west side of the park (one block away from our new homes, homeless people have settled with their tents, furniture, bikes, etc. On Tuesday 4/26, my family saw a man shooting heroin in his neck, in front of children playing outside. Then we left the park. Homeless people block the walkways. On Friday 7/1, I was forced to run in the city parking lot because homeless people were blocking the entrance to the park. I have contacted the City about this problem many times and I have never heard from them. When will is the city planning to clean the park and maintain it clean. My family do not want and it feels like we're at the point of watching Salt Lake City turn into just another tent city. It's time to take action and keep our city and parks safe for children and families to enjoy! Thanks, Katia Graftieaux

Regarding the water levels in the Great Salt Lake Council Comments Dear Council, I heard about your dire water situation on radio and got the following idea this morning that I hope may be of assistance. It's quite an expensive idea to accomplish, but it may be necessary in order for your population to survive. It would be a permanent fix as follows: If you could use a solar field to power a desalination plant on the California coast near the Pacific Ocean (your new aqueduct) you could keep the Great Salt Lake full. I have envisioned the design of a slow-cost, floating, solar water desalination plant that would go on the Pacific to serve your city. That is, a floating desalination plant. I'm an artist using a new low-cost generator that also came to my mind about the same time (early June 2022). Over time, the desalination plant would increase the salinity of the ocean (which wouldn't be much of a problem because ocean water has a lower salinity than the Great Salt Lake), and both, the salinity and water levels in the lake could be adjusted and maintained at desired levels if using this system. I would be happy to discuss this idea further. I live in Alberta and invented (and I am not an engineer but an artist) but has designed many special furnishings as well as a house package for the Third World). I would need to work with engineers for this one, in particular chemical, solar and marine, as well as inventors to help others like you who are also suffering life-altering or even, life-threatening drought.
